author: Robert Carr
description: Smoked paprika and lemon chicken with lemon-parsley brown basmati rice, roasted broccoli and red peppers, and a cool garlic-lemon yogurt sauce.
equipment: Two rimmed metal sheet pans, including an 18-by-13-inch pan for the vegetables
Saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, or a rice cooker
Chef's knife and separate cutting boards for produce and raw chicken
Shallow refrigerator- and freezer-safe containers and separate sauce cups, for meal prep

groceryIngredients.note: Plain, unseasoned chicken without added salt solution or brine; four roughly 6 oz raw portions.
Plain dry rice, not a seasoned mix; 1 standard US cup, about 180 g.
Floret weight after trimming; plain frozen florets also work, following the notes.
Large peppers, about 300 g total after removing stems and seeds.
Total for the chicken, vegetables, and sauce.
Two large lemons, for 2 tsp finely grated zest and 4 tbsp juice total.
One small clove, about 1/2 tsp finely grated, for the sauce.
Pure spice, not a salted seasoning blend.
Fine table salt: 5/8 tsp total for all four meals, about 3.75 g; do not substitute coarse salt by volume.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, plain and unseasoned, without added salt solution or brine
1 cup dry brown basmati rice, about 180 g; use a standard US measuring cup
1 3/4 cups water for the rice, or the amount specified on its package, plus small amounts as needed
1 lb (454 g) broccoli florets, cut into roughly 1 1/2-inch pieces
2 large red bell peppers, about 300 g after trimming, cut into 1-inch pieces
3 tablespoons olive oil, divided: 1 tablespoon chicken, 1 1/2 tablespoons vegetables, and 1/2 tablespoon sauce
2 large lemons, for 2 teaspoons finely grated zest and 4 tablespoons juice, divided
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, divided
1 small garlic clove, finely grated, about 1/2 teaspoon
1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, divided; not garlic salt
5/8 teaspoon fine table salt, about 3.75 g, divided: 3/8 teaspoon chicken, 1/8 teaspoon vegetables, and 1/8 teaspoon sauce
instructions: Start the rice first and continue with the remaining preparation while it cooks and rests. Heat a conventional oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C), with racks in the upper- and lower-middle positions. Rinse the rice and drain. Combine it with 1 3/4 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to a low simmer for about 40 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Use the rice package's liquid ratio and time when different; do not add butter, broth, or salt. If the rice is still firm and the pot is dry, add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, cover, and cook a little longer.

Wash and dry the vegetables, parsley, and lemons. Chop the vegetables and parsley, then measure 2 teaspoons lemon zest, avoiding the white pith, and 4 tablespoons juice. Before handling raw chicken, stir the yogurt, 1/2 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 2 tablespoons parsley, the grated garlic, and 1/8 teaspoon salt together in a clean bowl. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons water only if needed for a spoonable sauce. Refrigerate the sauce and keep its utensils separate from the chicken.

Toss the thoroughly dried broccoli and peppers with 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon oregano, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Spread on the vegetable pan in one layer with space between pieces, placing flat broccoli surfaces against the pan where possible. Roast on the upper-middle rack for about 25 to 35 minutes, checking from 20 minutes and tossing and rotating the pan around halfway through, until tender with browned edges. Do not pile the vegetables or cook them until blackened. Prepare the chicken during the first 8 to 10 minutes of roasting.

Pat the chicken dry; do not rinse it. Divide into four roughly equal portions and gently pound the thicker sections between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 3/4-inch thickness. Coat with 1 tablespoon olive oil, the smoked paprika and cumin, 1 teaspoon oregano, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 3/8 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon lemon zest, and the optional crushed red pepper. Spread on the second rimmed pan with space between pieces. Roast on the lower-middle rack for about 18 to 24 minutes, checking from 15 minutes. Remove each piece when its thickest part reaches 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), then rest on a clean plate for 5 minutes. Do not keep cooking a done piece just to darken its crust. Wash hands and clean surfaces and utensils after handling raw chicken.

Fluff the rested rice and fold in the remaining 1 teaspoon lemon zest, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and the remaining 2 tablespoons parsley. Drizzle 1 tablespoon lemon juice over the rested chicken and toss the roasted vegetables with the remaining 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Remove each component as it becomes ready rather than overcooking one while waiting for another. For meal prep, begin cooling finished components promptly as described in the notes, rather than leaving the rice in its pot.

Divide the chicken, rice, and vegetables evenly among four plates or shallow meal-prep containers. Serve with one quarter of the yogurt sauce, about 3 to 4 tablespoons per meal. Divide the cooked rice batch evenly rather than relying on an exact cooked volume. Keep sauce in separate refrigerated cups for meal prep and add it only after reheating.
notes: Allow about 60 to 65 minutes overall, with roughly 20 to 25 minutes of hands-on work. The rice cooks and rests while the other components are prepared; the oven time and chicken rest overlap the rice time. Oven performance, rice brand, and chicken thickness affect timing. Keep the chicken and vegetables on separate rimmed pans so they can be removed independently. If the vegetables do not fit in a single uncrowded layer, use additional pan space or roast in batches and allow more time.

The measured oil and salt cover the entire meal, including the rice, vegetables, and sauce; there is no extra salted cooking water, broth, or bottled dressing. Check the chicken label for added salt solution, use plain yogurt and unsalted spices, and measure fine table salt rather than substituting coarse or kosher salt by volume. Smoked paprika, browned vegetables, lemon zest, and the yogurt sauce provide the main flavor contrast. Taste a bite of the components together before adjusting the seasoning; the optional red pepper adds heat without changing the base recipe.

Sunday meal prep: For a conservative rice-storage plan, refrigerate only the portions that will be eaten within 24 hours of cooking and freeze the rest promptly after rapid cooling. This follows the UK Food Standards Agency's rice-specific advice. Divide the rice into shallow portions immediately after its covered rest; use a cold-water bath around a shallow metal container if needed, keeping water out of the food. Aim to cool and refrigerate or freeze rice within 1 hour after cooking. Do not leave it in the cooking pot or on the counter to cool completely. Refrigerate other cooked components within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 degrees F. Keep the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below and the freezer at 0 degrees F or below.

Freeze the cooled chicken, rice, and vegetables in individual portions, with room around containers for cold air to circulate until chilled. Keep the chicken and rice beside rather than buried under the vegetables. Label the cooking date and aim to use frozen portions within 2 months for quality. Store the yogurt sauce separately in the refrigerator and use within 3 to 4 days, or sooner if an ingredient's storage instructions require it. Make fresh sauce for later freezer meals; it can separate and become grainy if frozen. Frozen and reheated vegetables will be softer than freshly roasted ones.

Microwave reheating: Thaw one frozen meal overnight in the refrigerator and use within 24 hours of thawing. Remove the sauce cup. Cut the cooked chicken into thick slices for more even heating, add 1 to 2 tablespoons water mainly over the rice, and cover with a microwave-safe vented lid. Heat at medium to medium-high power in 60-second intervals, stirring the rice and vegetables and turning the chicken between intervals. Use shorter intervals near the end. Allow a 1-minute stand, then check several places with a thermometer: chicken, rice, and vegetables must all reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Continue heating if needed, then add the cold sauce and eat immediately. Reheat only the portion being eaten and reheat rice only once; reheating does not make improperly stored rice safe.

Frozen vegetables: Plain frozen broccoli can replace fresh florets by weight; follow its package cooking directions. If oven cooking is suitable, roast from frozen and allow about a 5- to 10-minute head start before adding fresh peppers, then cook until tender and browned. For a simpler alternative, cook plain frozen vegetables according to their package and toss with the same measured oil, seasonings, and finishing lemon juice. Do not add more salt or oil merely because the vegetables were frozen, and expect a softer texture than fresh roasted vegetables.

Rice cooker option: Use the cooker's instructions for brown rice instead of the saucepan step. Measure the recipe's 1 standard US cup of dry rice rather than silently substituting a smaller rice-cooker cup; follow the machine's matching water guidance and start early enough for its full cycle. Stir in lemon and parsley after cooking. For a quicker dinner, properly cooled and frozen plain brown rice may be reheated with the meal, but serve it then rather than cooling and reheating it again for another meal.

For eight meals, double the ingredients but use more pan space or cook in batches instead of crowding the same pans. Keep the raw garlic in the sauce modest, since its flavor becomes more noticeable as it rests. Plain nonfat Greek yogurt can replace 2% in the same amount; it makes a tangier sauce. The yogurt sauce contains milk.
title: Smoky Lemon Chicken with Brown Rice and Roasted Vegetables
